transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-03-17 15:00 UTC; Duration: 48 minutes; Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Anika Rao (CTO, Sierra), Markus Lee (Platform Lead), Priya Nair (InfoSec), Leo Park (SRE).

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
- Sierra HealthStream is evaluating whether Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, or Private fits their HIPAA workflow for realtime chat summarization and triage. Primary concerns: p95 latency for streaming responses, steady-state token/sec economics, concurrency targets, and compliance controls (SOC2/HIPAA).
- They currently plan for a steady 600 concurrent chat sessions with spikes to 2,500 over 10-minute windows. Goal p95 for short responses ~200ms, for longer streaming (summaries) p95 ~800ms.
- Agreed next steps: security docs, benchmark harness, scheduling pilot for Dedicated but explore Hosted fallback.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Okay, hey everyone, thank you for carving out time. I'm Maya, account lead for Redwood Inference. With me is Diego, our solutions engineer. Quick sound check?
[00:18] Anika Rao: Sounds good. Hi, Maya. Hi, Diego. Anika here.
[00:22] Markus Lee: Markus, yes, good to meet you all.
[00:25] Diego Morales: Hey Anika, hey team. Quick agenda: we want to understand your workload, p95 targets, concurrency and if there are any hard compliance constraints that push you to Private.
[00:34] Priya Nair: I'll jump in on the compliance side. We are a covered entity, HIPAA applies, and we need audited logs, KMS with customer-managed keys ideally. SOC2 already in our vendor bar.
[00:44] Leo Park: From infra, we care about cold starts and streaming stability — we run a lot of live transcriptions and short user queries.

[01:02] Maya Chen: Great. Maybe Anika you can start with the product flow and traffic shape? How many concurrent users, average tokens per session, burst patterns?
[01:12] Anika Rao: Sure. Our main feature is clinician-facing chat and automated visit summaries. Typical chat is 60 to 120 tokens per message, summary jobs are around 1,500 tokens. Steady-state is about 600 concurrent sessions across regions, but we have hourly spikes — think 2,000 to 2,500 concurrent over 5-10 minute windows during shift changes.
[01:35] Markus Lee: Important nuance: for triage we need sub-second feedback for short prompts. Ideally p95 under 200ms for one-shot clarifying prompts. For summaries we accept higher latency but p95 needs to be under 900ms so it doesn't block the clinician flow.
[01:52] Diego Morales: Got it. When you say p95 200ms, is that end-to-end including network and client-side processing, or strictly server token generation?
[02:01] Markus Lee: It's end-to-end. From UI send to first useful chunk streaming.
[02:06] Diego Morales: Okay that helps. For streaming scenarios we typically measure TTF (time-to-first-token) and TTR (time-to-rest) and then p95 across both.

[02:25] Maya Chen: On hosting preference — do you have an initial bias toward Hosted, Dedicated or Private?
[02:31] Anika Rao: We prefer Dedicated for performance predictability but compliance might push us to Private if KMS and VPC isolation are required. Hosted is attractive cost-wise but we worry about data residency and contractual obligations.
[02:43] Priya Nair: To clarify, we can accept Redwood's hosted if there is a BAAs and customer-managed key integration plus region tenancy. But if there are gaps, Private is our fallback.

[03:02] Diego Morales: Totally fair. On Dedicated we can reserve GPU pools for you, set autoscale and burst policies. Private gives you full control of the control plane and network. Hosted is the fastest to spin up.

[03:20] Markus Lee: Can you share-ish what token/sec we can expect for the sort of models we might run? We're considering a moderately-large open model, roughly 13B-ish, for summaries; smaller 6B-ish for chat.
[03:33] Diego Morales: For a 13B on accelerated GPUs with continuous batching and KV cache, we've seen steady-state decode throughput of ~80-120 tokens/sec per GPU for long-form sampling workloads, higher for greedy decoding. For 6B-chat, that can be 200-350 tokens/sec per GPU depending on batch sizing and quantization. But real numbers depend on sequence length distribution and your batching.
[03:58] Anika Rao: That variability worries us — how do you control p95 when batching yields higher throughput but increases latency for single-shot queries?
[04:07] Diego Morales: Great question. We do dynamic batching with latency SLO tiers — you can pin a route to low-latency mode which prioritizes single-request scheduling and smaller batches, or throughput mode which aggregates more requests. We also have prefix caching to reduce cost and latency for repeated context like patient metadata.
[04:28] Leo Park: Is prefix caching the one you call KV cache? We've seen notes where it was transcribed as K-V catch in other docs.
[04:34] Diego Morales: (laughs) Yes, KV cache — stores key/values between tokens for autoregressive loops to avoid recomputation. It helps a lot for multi-turn chat.

[04:50] [05:00] Markus Lee: Let's talk numbers framed by our p95 targets: when pinned to low-latency mode with smaller batch size, what p95 values are reasonable for the 6B chat for TTF and for a 13B single-pass summary?
[05:12] Diego Morales: Based on similar customers: 6B, low-latency mode, TTF p95 in hosted or dedicated can be in the 120–300ms range for short prompts (single chunk), assuming network RTT under ~80ms. For 13B summaries TTF will be higher — initial token might be 300–600ms p95 and full summary depends on tokens/sec.
[05:34] Anika Rao: You said network RTT — we have a hybrid infra with VPC peering to us-east1. Any guidance for placement?
[05:42] Diego Morales: Best is geo-proximity. If most of your traffic originates in us-east, put the serving pool there. Also Dedicated gives you reserved GPUs in a region which stabilizes latency SLOs.

[05:58] [06:15] Priya Nair: On encryption and key management — do you support customer-managed keys and HSM-backed KMS? Our legal is strict about key custody for PHI.
[06:25] Maya Chen: We do. For Private deployments you can bring your own KMS/HSM. For Dedicated we support KMS integrations and customer-managed keys in many cloud providers; we'll send the exact matrix. Hosted can integrate with CMKs in certain regions with supplemental contract.
[06:44] Priya Nair: Are audit logs structured in a way we can ingest into our SIEM?
[06:49] Diego Morales: Yes — we provide structured event logs, token-level cost metrics, and per-request traces. They can be pushed to your log collector or exported. There is a small retention tradeoff for hosted tiers.

[07:10] Markus Lee: On fallback — if Dedicated is saturated, do you route to Hosted or degrade?
[07:18] Diego Morales: You can configure smart routing rules. Typical pattern: primary route to Dedicated with canary fallback to Hosted or to a smaller model variant. That ensures availability while controlling cost.

[07:32] Anika Rao: Let's get concrete on the pilot. We'd like Redwood to help run a token/sec benchmark against our expected workload with our prompts. Does Redwood provide a harness or should we run it?
[07:42] Diego Morales: We can provide a benchmark harness and a runbook. Ideally you share a sample prompt set and sequence length distribution. We'll run tests against a Dedicated-like setup and a Hosted baseline and return results.

[08:00] Leo Park: We will need steps to reproduce locally as well because our security team will ask for the exact commands.
[08:06] Diego Morales: We'll include the CLI steps plus a small containerized test runner. Also a spreadsheet with expected cost per token assumptions.

[08:20] [08:40] Anika Rao: One blocker: BAAs and indemnity. Our procurement needs to know if Redwood will sign a BAA and if the data handling docs match HIPAA criteria.
[08:48] Maya Chen: Redwood has precedent BAAs with other healthcare customers; I'll loop in our contracts team and share template language. We'll send a redline-ready BAA and the security questionnaire.

[09:05] Priya Nair: There are also specific questions: do you store raw transcripts, and for how long? Can retention be set per-customer?
[09:13] Diego Morales: Retention is configurable per account. For Hosted we have default retention windows but can set zero-retention or customer-managed logging for Private. We'll include that in the security doc packet.

[09:30] Markus Lee: Back to performance — in streaming, do you support partial response prioritization? E.g., prefer to emit shorter, useful tokens early to satisfy UI p95?
[09:40] Diego Morales: Yes. Our runtime supports chunked streaming and you can control chunk size and maximum lookahead. That, along with early-stop heuristics, helps meet UI p95 while still producing coherent summaries.

[09:58] [10:15] Anika Rao: Hypothetical numbers — if we aim for p95 TTF of 200ms for 6B chat, and we have 600 steady concurrent sessions with spikes to 2,500, what's the rough Dedicated footprint? GPUs?
[10:28] Diego Morales: Rough ballpark: assuming each 6B session averages 50 tokens per interaction and low-latency mode with smaller batching, we might need 10–14 GPUs steady to hit p95 targets, with autoscale headroom to 30 GPUs during spikes. For 13B-heavy summarization, add dedicated workers for batch jobs or use a different pool. But this is very workload-dependent — we'll run a sizing run.
[10:50] Leo Park: That seems significant. Can you illustrate cost delta if we go Hosted vs Dedicated for that footprint?
[10:57] Maya Chen: We'll share a cost comparison sheet — Hosted often has higher per-token price but no infra ops, Dedicated lowers run-rate but has committed capacity pricing. We'll model your actual concurrency and tokens.

[11:16] Markus Lee: Also curious on quantization — are your recommended quantized variants functionally equivalent for summaries? We worried about subtle quality regression.
[11:26] Diego Morales: For many open models, 4-bit or nf4 quant can be nearly indistinguishable for general Summarization. We do evals on your prompt set to detect regressions. Redwood Optimize will flag quality deltas and recommend model/quant profiles.

[11:44] Anika Rao: Let's discuss timeline and stakeholders. We want a pilot in 2 weeks if possible — security sign-off permitting.
[11:53] Maya Chen: Two weeks is tight but we've done accelerated pilots. Next steps from our side: send security package, benchmark harness, and propose pilot dates by end of this week.

[12:05] [12:30] Priya Nair: One more thing — do you offer SAML SSO / RBAC for role separation? Our compliance requires just-in-time access controls and auditable admin actions.
[12:39] Diego Morales: Yes; SSO via SAML/OIDC and granular RBAC are available. For Private you manage identity through your IdP. For Hosted we integrate with SSO and provide enterprise RBAC.

[12:54] Anika Rao: For the pilot, we'd like a test where we measure: 1) TTF p95 for chat, 2) end-to-end summary time p95, 3) tokens/sec throughput at steady and peak, and 4) failover behavior when the primary pool is saturated.
[13:12] Maya Chen: That's a solid scope — Diego will own the benchmark config, we'll run in your staging environment or a mirrored workload depending on network.

[13:25] [13:45] Diego Morales: A couple of practical notes: 1) instrument client-side timestamps for accurate E2E p95, 2) keep network RTT samples, 3) provide representative prompt corpus and streaming chunk expectations. We'll feed back per-route suggestions (batch size, model variant, quant settings).

[14:00] Leo Park: About instrumentation — do you ingest our traces or should we push traces to you?
[14:06] Diego Morales: Either works. For the pilot it's easiest if you push anonymized traces to a secure bucket we can access. We'll anonymize PHI before analysis.

[14:19] Anika Rao: Is there an automated way to test cold-start latency? We care about cold paths when autoscaling from zero.
[14:27] Diego Morales: Yes — the harness can simulate scale from idle and measure coldstart p95. Dedicated with warm pools minimizes cold-starts, while hosted with reserved capacity or warm pools also helps.

[14:40] [15:00] Priya Nair: I want to flag encryption-in-flight to our auditors. Is TLS mutual mandated or optional?
[15:07] Maya Chen: Mutual TLS is available for Private and Dedicated. For Hosted we enforce TLS and can support mTLS per customer request.

[15:20] Markus Lee: Great. Anything else on routing/fallback semantics? How deterministic are the fallbacks?
[15:27] Diego Morales: You can set routing rules in the Console — deterministic priority lists with weights, and health checks that trigger failover. We also provide observability to verify fallback paths and the reason codes.

[15:40] [15:50] Anika Rao: Okay let's surface the main risks from our POV: 1) quality regression with quantization, 2) time to sign BAA, 3) ability to meet strict p95 E2E under spikes.
[15:59] Maya Chen: Fair. We'll mitigate: run quality evals on your prompts, legal to share BAA template this week, and run stress/surge tests in the pilot to validate p95.

[16:12] Markus Lee: Can you give an example of a canary rollout strategy if we deploy model updates? We need to avoid regressions in production.
[16:20] Diego Morales: The Console supports canary percent rollouts, automatic rollback on quality regressions or latency regressions defined by you, and A/B test hooks. We'll detail the rollout policy template.

[16:34] [16:50] Anika Rao: For the pilot tech contacts — Markus and Leo will be the leads. Priya will handle compliance gate.
[16:57] Maya Chen: Noted. I'll include those contacts.

[17:05] Diego Morales: Quick follow-up on metrics: for the benchmark we'll produce a CSV with TTF p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and cost per 1M tokens.
[17:15] Leo Park: Perfect.

[17:25] [17:40] Priya Nair: Anything about SLAs — uptime, support response?
[17:45] Maya Chen: For Dedicated we offer SLA commitments with higher support tiers. Hosted has standard uptime SLAs; we'll attach SLA docs. Private is negotiated as part of the enterprise contract.

[17:58] Anika Rao: Ok, if we get good numbers in the Dedicated pilot, is it straightforward to expand into multi-region? We want active-active between us-east and europe-west eventually.
[18:08] Diego Morales: Yes — Redwood supports multi-region deployments with smart routing and sticky sessions if needed. Active-active is supported; we can model cross-region latencies in the pilot.

[18:22] Maya Chen: Great. I'll summarize next steps and action items.

[18:30] Maya Chen: Action items recapped: I'll send security and BAA templates; Diego sends benchmark harness and runbook; Markus/Leo share request patterns and sample prompts; Priya consolidates compliance questions — target dates in the calendar invite.

[18:47] Anika Rao: Sounds good. One more ask: can you include a sample cost estimate that shows committed Dedicated discount scenarios?
[18:55] Maya Chen: Yes, we will include committed vs pay-as-you-go scenarios with runtime assumptions.

[19:05] [19:20] Markus Lee: Thanks everyone. Quick note — we may also want to compare a hybrid pattern where summaries run on Dedicated batch workers and chat runs on Hosted.
[19:31] Diego Morales: That's a common optimization — batch offload for heavy summaries, real-time on dedicated low-latency pool. We'll include that in the comparison.

[19:45] Anika Rao: Thanks. Any final questions?
[19:50] Priya Nair: No final questions from InfoSec.
[19:53] Leo Park: All good.
[19:55] Maya Chen: Thank you very much. We'll follow up by end of day with all the artifacts.
[20:01] Anika Rao: Appreciate it. Bye.

End of transcript.
